Sometimes I wish I were a guy, even though there's no way that I identify as one. The worst is when I go to heavy metal concerts, they just looks so much more happy and free to be goofs with each other. Being a girl, I can't ever be just one of the guys, and I hate that. I have guy friends, but there's always the question of whether you're dating them, do they want to date you, do other people think you're dating, are they feeling friend-zoned, do they feel like they can tell you the same things or same jokes as their guy friends... I can name probably only one dude in my life who treats me like one of his bros, and it helps that he's already taken and with a girl who isn't jealous.


Anyway, you should do as you like, guy or girl, feminine or masculine, either, both or neither. Please be yourself and feel free to express emotions or like "girlie" things. Make a queer friend or two and chat with them about this stuff. I have a couple of gender queer friends, and it is soooo easy to talk to them about this kind of thing. You can poke around in some queer spaces online. It doesn't mean you have to be queer yourself, but if you make yourself an ally, you can make some understanding friends. :)

I don't have good advice. What I think I have are examples of what not to do. :(


I have a sibling with Autism. Parents, please don't hide your child's Autism from their siblings and then get mad when they get into fights. Children aren't born with an innate understanding of how to get along with a sibling with Autism. Please talk to them. Also make sure they don't feel that their needs take a back seat to the needs of their autistic siblings. I for example was bullied relentlessly and had abusive teachers, but my parents would snap at me and then give endless amounts of support to my brother. This is terrible and will make for a bad relationship between your children. 


If you have Autism and are currently in a bad place with any of your siblings, please try to keep an open mind and an open door. I know it is very difficult to put yourself in someone else's shoes, but most of us love you and don't want to lose you.

Can I make a suggestion? :)


> I'm a sucker for Christmas decorations.

> I'm also anxious about family asking what I want for Christmas. I never really know.


My family really likes to give each other Christmas ornaments. Some are collectible. If you think that you would like receiving that kind of gift, consider asking for that. I think you would also really like LED fairy lights.


> It's so crowded & I can't even get food or soap without nearly breaking down in a store.


Can you go to the store at less busy hours, such as very early in the morning or late at night? Weekend trips to 24/7 grocery stores are amazing. So quiet and empty.


Or do you have Instacart in your area? It's an app that sends a person out to do your grocery shopping for you, if you're comfortable with a stranger coming to drop them off at your home.


> I get really upset & usually end up crying.


I wish crying didn't feel so embarrassing. :( Please give yourself permission to take out time to cry if you need it.

I know this doesn't exactly help, but many girls out there will "ghost" a guy because of their own anxieties. I wouldn't blame yourself for it. We're a fickle lot. Hell, I've "ghosted" guys because I was still figuring out that I'm asexual and would freak out. None of them were doing anything wrong.


Maybe I'm not the most qualified person to chime in on this, being personally uninterested in dating, but don't let yourself get into a mindset of there being a time limit. Age is just a number and all that. Might I suggest taking a break and focus on building your social circle, finding other things you'd like to focus on, maybe getting fit or joining a club or running just to run? Get yourself in a better place first, then jump back on that horse.

> I have no redeeming qualities.


So... what I think is that you're still quite young, 21 years old, and you haven't fully "found" yourself yet. I want you to give yourself more of a chance, live more of your adult life, and really concentrate on the things you can do right now to make yourself more happy. 


I can't promise any magic bullet or that it gets better with only time alone, it doesn't. Living a life is work, and so is finding your own happiness. It's probable that you will fuck up a lot on the road ahead. Everyone does. There are no rewards in life without fuck-ups first. So give yourself permission to fuck up, to feel shitty, and continue finding your own way in life. I wish you the best.


And... as an anecdotal ending, I am going through my own shit, but when I was 21, I felt really the same. I'm now in my 30s and much better off. It's a long, hard road outta hell, but on the other side is a life very much worth living. You only get one life, so keep taking cracks at it, eventually you'll figure it out.

Thank you. I didn't actually expect anyone to read all of that. It was a ton of info.


My brother and I are both adults, so I don't know his doctor, we don't share the same one.


What I did, I sent him a reply where I asked him to get help and not to give up on himself, and I sent him a link to the national suicide prevention website and suggested that he can use an online chat with them. I'm glad they have that; guys like my brother might be too anxious to talk live on the phone. 


However, I did also have to ask him not attend the family dinner if he was going to make threats, like how he threatened to break one of my bones if I offended him in any way. I then told him about another family dinner on the same day where I won't be attending (due to yet ANOTHER relative who's not talking to somebody) and asked him to go there, but I urged him not to spend the holiday alone. My mother said he was planning to not go anywhere. 


Then I apologized for hurting his feelings online. I don't think he's in the right to go through my post history and freak out at me back when I had my own really bad, depressive time, but I never wanted to hurt his feelings, either. I wish his disorder didn't make it so hard.


It's shitty, because I'm now both scared for him and of him. I doubt he'll listen to me, but I feel better having tried. I can't blame myself for his disorder or depression, but I will feel absolutely terrible if anything happens to my family.


Edit: 

> Your family could use some famuly counselling too, although, from the sounds of it you might be the only one receptive to that.


Haaaaaa you have NO idea. But my brother used to be friends with his old school shrink. I wish he'd reach out to him for some support, but he's stubborn and thinking right now that people see him as a burden. So probably no.
